        - heading "PHASE LINE (x′ = f(x))" [level=3]
        - heading "TRAJECTORY (solution of x′ = −x(x+1)(x−2))" [level=3]
        - complementary:
          - generic: x₀ = -1.40
          - paragraph: lim x(t) = -1
          - text: Converges to equilibrium
          - generic: x = -1 (stable)
      - heading "CLASSIFICATION OF EQUILIBRIA" [level=2]
      - article:
        - heading "x = -1" [level=3]: x = -1
        - text: Stable (Attracting)
        - paragraph:
          - text: Trajectories nearby move toward −1.
          - text: f(x) changes sign at this point.
      - article:
        - heading "x = 0" [level=3]: x = 0
        - text: Unstable (Repelling)
        - paragraph:
          - text: Trajectories move away from 0.
          - text: f(x) changes sign at this point.
      - article:
        - heading "x = 2" [level=3]: x = 2
        - text: Stable (Attracting)
        - paragraph:
          - text: Trajectories nearby move toward 2.
          - text: f(x) changes sign at this point.
      - article:
        - heading "WHY THIS WORKS" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Equilibria occur where f(x*) = 0. Their stability is determined by the sign of f(x) on each side.
        - paragraph:
          - text: • If f goes from + to − → Stable
          - text: • If f goes from − to + →
          - emphasis: Unstable
          - text: • If f does not change sign → Semi-stable
        - paragraph: The potential V satisfies V′(x)=−f(x). Stable equilibria are local minima of V.
      - article:
        - heading "GOVERNING RULE" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "Autonomous 1D system: x′=f(x)"
        - text: "Equilibrium: f(x*)=0"
        - text: "Stability test:"
        - text: • f′(x*) < 0 → Stable
        - text: • f′(x*) > 0 → Unstable
        - text: • f′(x*) = 0 → Use sign test
      - article:
        - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]:
          - text: COMMON MISCONCEPTION
        - text: “Minima of the graph of f(x) are stable.”
        - paragraph: Not necessarily. Stability depends on the sign change of f, not on the shape of f itself.
      - article:
        - heading "TRY IT YOURSELF" [level=2]
        - paragraph:
          - text: Given f(x)=2x(x−1)²(x−3).
          - text: 1) Find all equilibria. 2) Classify each one using a sign chart.
        - button "Check my answer"
      - article:
        - heading "Answer (self-check)" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Complete the sign chart, then check your classification.
      - button "Need a hint?":
        - text: Need a hint?
